original_question: In an autosomal recessive genetic syndrome characterized by deafness, onychodystrophy, osteodystrophy, and intellectual disability, which long bones in the hands and feet exhibit abnormal shapes?

final_qi.question: In an autosomal recessive genetic syndrome characterized by deafness, onychodystrophy, osteodystrophy, and intellectual disability, which long bones in the hands and feet exhibit abnormal shapes?
final_qi.long_answer: In DOOR syndrome (Deafness-Onychodystrophy-Osteodystrophy-Intellectual disability), radiographs consistently reveal hypoplastic or misshapen phalanges—the long bones that form the fingers and toes—while other skeletal elements are relatively spared. These phalangeal abnormalities constitute the osteodystrophy component of the autosomal-recessive disorder.

final_answer.long_answer: The autosomal-recessive DOOR (Deafness-Onychodystrophy-Osteodystrophy-Intellectual disability) syndrome is characterized radiologically by dysplasia of the long bones of the digits—the phalanges of the fingers and toes—which are shortened, broadened, or otherwise malformed.
